text: There is a lot of confusion with the Devs in 2026.
There are so many programming languages to choose from.
So many AI tools are being used.
There are endless new frameworks and you get the opposite advice with your career.
I understand it is very difficult to choose what to do, and you know what the crazy part is?
In today's date, AI can write thousands of lines of code, that is for sure true.
But if you look at the quality of code, it is coming down.
Companies are not able to keep their code working.
So the question is, what are the basic skills that you need in AI era?
What are the skills that will actually pay you well?
And what are the new AI tools that you can skip and you won't have to care?
And the answer to these things that you won't get in social media hype.
The real answer to these things is in real-world job market data or in hiring trends.
If you want to make your long-lasting career in software development,
then you have to ignore marketing hype and focus on what is going on in the real world.
AI has brought a lot of changes, the way Devs used to work and the way they work now.
But the need for basic coding skills has not been replaced.
In fact, talking about real-world data is a big gap.
How do we use AI tools and how much trust do we have on AI in those two?
According to the DEV survey of the 2020 Stack Overflow, 84% of people use AI every day in their day-to-day tasks.
But only 29% actually trust the code written by AI.
Apart from that, 66% of the devs are frustrated that AI has written a lot of code,
but it takes hours to fix the one part that is wrong.
It is not as valuable to memorize the syntax in today's day-to-day tasks as it is valuable to understand the system.
AI will set you up in a basic server, but it can't recognize the rules, security needs, user limits.
The biggest risk for companies today is that you just copy and paste the code without looking at it.
And you can't understand what's going on in it.
This is called cognitive debt.
The entire team is saying that the code is working, but I don't know how it's working.
Don't touch it, it will get spoiled.
But the real problem is that it has to be updated.
I don't understand.
According to recent data, the code bases are getting worse.
They used to be, but they are getting worse.
According to the Git Clear report of 2025, it has read 211 million lines of code.
In which my code churn was made.
It means that only two weeks in between, a lot of code is being written, deleted, and changed.
Which was before, but now it's doubled, which is now 7.1%.
Because the devs have started using AI and the copy-paste has increased by 48%.
Now, people are going all-time low to clean up the code and maintain it.
So, the company doesn't want you to just fill in the code.
